items.question: Why is Imran’s mother planning a special dinner?

options.B: It is a school sports day

items.question: Why does his mother make a shopping list?

options.D: Every item has the same price

items.question: In Section A, how many eggs are already at home?
items.explanation: This is existing stock, not the dozen more he proposes buying.

items.question: In Section B, what does Imran do before asking for sugar and milk?
items.explanation: The stage direction says that he looks at the list.

items.question: What kind of bag does Imran request in Section B?
items.explanation: Both paper and jute are accepted in his request.

items.question: What total does the salesperson state in Section B?
items.explanation: 535 is the bill; 550 is the amount paid.

items.question: How much change does the salesperson give Imran?
items.explanation: The stated change is consistent with 550 minus 535.

activities.instruction: Answer using the cited text. Equivalent accurate wording is acceptable; support interpretations with details.

items.question: Compare the potato quantities in Sections A and B, and identify an additional item in B.
items.modelAnswer: Section A requests half a kilogram of potatoes; Section B requests two kilograms. Section B also adds salt, which Section A did not request.

items.question: How much milk and sugar does Imran ask for in Section B?
items.modelAnswer: He asks for one litre of milk and one kilogram of sugar.

items.question: How many different kinds of goods does Imran request in Section B? Name them.
items.modelAnswer: He requests nine kinds: beans, tomatoes, potatoes, cauliflowers, eggs, salt, oil, sugar and milk.

items.question: Does the dialogue state why Imran asks for a paper or jute bag?
items.modelAnswer: No explicit reason is stated. A reader may suggest reducing plastic-bag use, but this is an inference, not a stated motive.

items.question: What does the salesperson say about plastic bags?
items.modelAnswer: The salesperson says that they do not use plastic bags in that shop.

activities.instruction: Write an original shopping dialogue. Ask for goods, confirm a price, pay and receive the correct change.

modelAnswer.speaker: Customer
modelAnswer.text: Good morning. May I have two notebooks, please?

modelAnswer.speaker: Shopkeeper
modelAnswer.text: Certainly. They are thirty taka each.

modelAnswer.speaker: Customer
modelAnswer.text: That makes sixty taka altogether. Here is one hundred taka.

modelAnswer.speaker: Shopkeeper
modelAnswer.text: Thank you. Here are your notebooks and forty taka change.

modelAnswer.speaker: Customer
modelAnswer.text: Thank you. I have brought my own bag.

modelAnswer.speaker: Shopkeeper
modelAnswer.text: You’re welcome. Have a good day.

activities.note: Original fictional prices; not current market-price claims or additions to Imran’s purchase.
assessment: Addresses the task with relevant details
Uses a clear sequence and connected sentences

limitations: Initial Draft pool, not exhaustive chapter quotas or a complete model paper.
